spec.name: Agent Trust eXtension
spec.version: 1.0 (v1.1 fixtures included: JCS/RFC 8785 TBS signing, declaredPurpose)

verifiers.coverage: full: Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) hybrid signatures, v1.0 pipe canonical form and v1.1 JCS(TBS)
full: Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204, via dilithium-py) hybrid signatures, v1.0 pipe canonical form and v1.1 JCS(TBS) via vendored RFC 8785

additionalGates.name: jcs-byte-agreement
additionalGates.description: three independent canonicalizers (Go gowebpki/jcs, vendored Python RFC 8785, TypeScript erdtman/canonicalize) and the v1.1 TBS projection of both verifiers (verifiers/go, verifiers/python) must reproduce each vector's pinned canonical bytes exactly; the gate needs the Python verifier's dependencies

notCovered.item: Distinct signer-authority count (ATX core.md section 1.3 step 7)
notCovered.reason: no fixture carries verified signatures from more than one distinct authority, and the fixture format has no field for the required trust level that step 7's condition reads, so a verifier that omits step 7 entirely passes the suite; a length-of-issuerChain test is not step 7 (the spec says the chain length MUST NOT be counted) and implementations MUST self-attest this requirement until a fixture exists for it

notCovered.item: k-of-n threshold issuance (ATX core.md section 3.1 step 8: cosignatures from 2 of 3 key holders)
notCovered.reason: the fixture format has no field for the required signature count and neither reference verifier reads one: both require every declared signature to verify and at least one to be present, so the threshold fixture's credential cut to one of its three signatures is accepted, and a verifier that checks only the first signature passes the threshold fixture

notCovered.item: Cosignature requirements (ATX core.md section 7: federation cosigning, and the root cosignature at trust level 4)
notCovered.reason: the threshold fixture pins three signatures over the signing bytes, each of which must verify; no fixture asserts that a trust level 4 credential carries the root cosignature or that a federated issuance carries its peer's cosignature
the revoked-crl-only fixture pins the verdict for an agentId that is on the verifier's CRL; no fixture exercises the 5-minute cache bound or a stale-CRL window
no fixture models a monitor and the conformance verifiers do not consult a log

requirements.name: atx-v1/baseline-valid-hybrid
requirements.requirement: §1.3 step 5: every declared signature verifies, the ML-DSA-65 signature included, so a v1.0 hybrid credential is accepted

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.0 credential carrying both an Ed25519 signature and an ML-DSA-65 signature over the same canonical payload. This is the hybrid signing path the ATX v1.0 spec mandates. A spec-conformant verifier MUST verify BOTH signatures and ACCEPT only when both are valid. The ML-DSA-65 signature value is a raw FIPS 204 ML-DSA-65 signature (3309 bytes decoded) over the same canonical bytes as the Ed25519 signature; no container or combined-blob framing is used.

requirements.name: atx-v1/baseline-valid
requirements.requirement: §1.3 step 8: a v1.0 credential whose one Ed25519 signature, made with its issuer's key, verifies over the legacy canonical bytes passes every step and is accepted

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: A baseline ATX v1.0 credential issued by a single trusted authority with one Ed25519 signature. Verifier MUST ACCEPT.

requirements.name: atx-v1/cross-issuer-key
requirements.requirement: §1.3 step 4, key eligibility: under atcVersion 1.0 only a key resolved for the issuerDid is eligible, so a signature made with another trusted authority's key is a signature failure

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.0 credential issued by the primary authority (issuerDid = did:opena2a:authority:opena2a.org) but signed by a DIFFERENT trusted authority's key (did:opena2a:authority:partner.example#key-1). The signature is valid over the canonical payload and the signing authority is independently trusted, yet that key is not controlled by the credential's issuer and is not in its issuerChain. A verifier MUST bind each signature to a key controlled by the credential's issuer and MUST REJECT with a signature-validation reason, so a trusted authority cannot impersonate another. A verifier that tries every configured key would wrongly ACCEPT.

requirements.name: atx-v1/expired
requirements.requirement: §1.3 step 2: a credential whose expiresAt is earlier than the verifier's clock is rejected

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An otherwise-valid ATX whose ExpiresAt is earlier than the verifier's pinned clock. Verifier MUST REJECT with an expiry reason.

requirements.name: atx-v1/malformed-schema
requirements.requirement: §1.3 step 1: a credential whose atcVersion (2.0) is not a supported schema version is rejected

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX whose atcVersion claims a version (2.0) that is not the v1.0 supported by this conformance suite. Verifier MUST REJECT at step 1 (schema-version check) with an unsupported-version reason. NOTE: the signature is computed over v1.0 canonical bytes, whose eleventh field is the literal "1.0" independent of the credential's atcVersion field; the fixture is otherwise well formed so that a verifier can demonstrate it rejects on the schema-version check alone.

requirements.name: atx-v1/revoked-crl-only
requirements.requirement: §1.3 step 6: an agentId listed on the verifier's CRL is rejected although the credential's own revoked flag is false

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.0 credential whose own revoked flag is false and whose AgentID appears in the verifier's CRL. It is the accepted baseline in every other respect: a trusted issuer, unexpired, one Ed25519 signature that verifies. CRL membership is the only thing that revokes it, so a verifier that reads the credential's revoked flag and never consults the CRL wrongly accepts. The flag is outside the signed bytes of both signing forms, so it can be cleared on a revoked credential without breaking the signature; the CRL entry cannot. Verifier MUST REJECT with a revocation reason that names the CRL.

requirements.name: atx-v1/revoked
requirements.requirement: §3.3 step 7: a credential its issuing node marked revoked is rejected; its revoked flag is set and its agentId is also on the verifier's CRL

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: A previously-valid ATX whose credential-level Revoked flag is set and whose AgentID also appears in the verifier's CRL. Verifier MUST REJECT with revocation reason. Both rejection paths are exercised.

requirements.name: atx-v1/tampered-signature
requirements.requirement: §1.3 step 4: an Ed25519 signature that does not verify over the legacy canonical bytes is a signature failure

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX whose Ed25519 signature has been flipped by one bit after signing. All other fields are unchanged. Verifier MUST REJECT with a signature-validation reason.

requirements.name: atx-v1/threshold-2of3-cosignature
requirements.requirement: §1.3 step 5: every declared signature verifies, here three Ed25519 signatures by three keys, so the credential is accepted; the 2-of-3 threshold of §3.1 step 8 is not tested

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX cosigned by all three keys of a 2-of-3 threshold issuer (primary plus two cosigners). All three signatures are Ed25519 and cover the same canonical payload. Verifier MUST ACCEPT. A spec-conformant verifier additionally MUST validate at least two of the three signatures for trust level 4.

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/baseline-valid-hybrid
requirements.requirement: §1.3 step 5: every declared signature verifies, the ML-DSA-65 signature included, so a v1.1 hybrid credential is accepted

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.1 credential carrying both an Ed25519 signature and an ML-DSA-65 signature over the SAME JCS(TBS) bytes. A spec-conformant verifier MUST verify both and ACCEPT.

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/baseline-valid
requirements.requirement: §1.3a.2: a v1.1 credential whose one Ed25519 signature verifies over JCS(TBS) is accepted

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: A baseline ATX v1.1 credential. The single Ed25519 signature covers JCS(TBS) per atx-spec core.md §1.3a.2, so capabilities, scanSummary, issuerChain, publisher, and behavioralProfile are integrity-protected. Verifier MUST ACCEPT. The canonical bytes equal the jcs-vectors baseline vector.

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/case-variant-member
requirements.requirement: §1.3 step 1: parsing the credential rejects two member names that fold to one field (TRUSTLEVEL and trustLevel) as PARSE_ERROR before any field is read (§12)

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.1 credential carrying a decoy top-level TRUSTLEVEL member (value 9) injected before the signed trustLevel member (value 4) — two names that fold to the same field. Go's encoding/json resolves struct fields case-insensitively last-wins, so it collapses the pair to the signed trustLevel=4: a lenient Go verifier ACCEPTs, silently carrying a stray fold-colliding TRUSTLEVEL member. The same bytes read differently under other conforming parsers: a case-insensitive first-wins parser reads 9, and a case-sensitive parser (this suite's Python json.loads) keeps both as distinct members, reading trustLevel=4 alongside a separate TRUSTLEVEL=9. A case-SENSITIVE duplicate check flags neither. Because encoding/json's field folding makes the credential mean different things to different conforming parsers — the RFC 8259 §4 first-wins/last-wins parser divergence the strict parse exists to close — verifiers MUST fold member names and REJECT fold-colliding members with PARSE_ERROR before interpreting any field. Reference: foldKey in verifiers/go and verifiers/python (atx-conformance#16).

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/cross-issuer-key
requirements.requirement: §1.3 step 4, key eligibility: under atcVersion 1.1 a key is eligible only for the issuerDid or a trusted issuer the signed issuerChain names, so a signature made with a trusted authority's key outside both is a signature failure

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.1 credential issued by the primary authority but signed by a different trusted authority's key (partner.example). The secondary authority is trusted and its key is configured, and the signature is valid over JCS(TBS), but the secondary is neither the issuer nor present in the signed issuerChain. A spec-conformant verifier binds each signature to a key controlled by the issuer, or by an authority that is both named in the signed issuerChain and in the verifier's trusted issuers, and MUST REJECT with a signature-validation reason.

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/declared-purpose-array-injected
requirements.requirement: §1.3a.2 rule 5: a present non-object declaredPurpose value enters the TBS verbatim, so an array added after signing is a signature failure

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.1 credential signed with no declaredPurpose, carrying an attacker-appended ARRAY declaredPurpose value. Non-object values are included in the TBS verbatim (atx-spec §1.3a.2 rule 5), so the recomputed canonical bytes no longer match the signature and the verifier MUST REJECT with a signature-validation reason. A verifier that normalizes non-object values away would accept unsigned purpose content riding a valid signature.

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/declared-purpose-empty-whitespace
requirements.requirement: §1.3a.2 rule 5: an empty declaredPurpose object, whatever whitespace it is written with, is treated as absent and left out of the TBS

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.1 credential signed with no declaredPurpose, carrying a whitespace-empty declaredPurpose object ({ }) appended after signing. Emptiness is a JSON-parse-level property (atx-spec §1.3a.2 rule 5): any serialization of the empty object is the empty object, treated as absent and omitted from the TBS, so the signature still verifies. Verifier MUST ACCEPT. A verifier that compares the raw byte string against "{}" instead of parsing wrongly includes the value and REJECTs.

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/declared-purpose-number-injected
requirements.requirement: §1.3a.2 rule 5: a present non-object declaredPurpose value enters the TBS verbatim, so a number that is not an integer, added after signing, is a signature failure

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.1 credential signed with no declaredPurpose, carrying an attacker-appended NUMBER declaredPurpose value, 1.5, which is not an integer. Non-object values are included in the TBS verbatim (atx-spec §1.3a.2 rule 5), so the recomputed canonical bytes no longer match the signature and the verifier MUST REJECT with a signature-validation reason. JCS writes a number that is not an integer with the number serialization of RFC 8785 §3.2.2.3; a verifier whose serializer does not implement it has no canonical bytes for a signature to verify over, and its expected outcome is the same REJECT.

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/declared-purpose-string-injected
requirements.requirement: §1.3a.2 rule 5: a present non-object declaredPurpose value enters the TBS verbatim, so a string added after signing is a signature failure

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.1 credential signed with no declaredPurpose, carrying an attacker-appended STRING declaredPurpose value. Non-object values are included in the TBS verbatim (atx-spec §1.3a.2 rule 5), so the recomputed canonical bytes no longer match the signature and the verifier MUST REJECT with a signature-validation reason.

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/declared-purpose-valid
requirements.requirement: §1.5: a present declaredPurpose object is signed as part of JCS(TBS) (§1.3a.2 rule 5), and a credential carrying one is accepted

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: A baseline ATX v1.1 credential carrying a populated declaredPurpose (atx-spec §1.5): vocabVersion, statement, category, taskScopes, capabilityJustification, autonomy, dataScopes, egressScopes. declaredPurpose is the one presence-based TBS member (§1.3a.2 rule 5); when present it is signed as part of JCS(TBS). Verifier MUST ACCEPT. Canonical bytes equal the jcs-vectors 08-declared-purpose vector.

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/duplicate-purpose-member
requirements.requirement: §1.3 step 1: parsing the credential rejects an object member repeated at any depth (RFC 8259 §4) as PARSE_ERROR before any field is read (§12)

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.1 credential whose declaredPurpose bytes contain the category member twice: a decoy (customer-support) followed by the signed value (financial-operations). The Ed25519 signature is REAL and covers the last-wins interpretation, so a lenient last-wins parser sees a verifying credential while a first-wins parser sees different content — the classic RFC 8259 §4 duplicate-member smuggling split. Because the entire ATX credential feeds the signed canonical form (JCS(TBS), §1.3a.2), verifiers MUST strict-parse the credential object and REJECT duplicate members at any depth with PARSE_ERROR, before interpreting any field. A verifier that parses last-wins without a duplicate check wrongly ACCEPTs; a first-wins verifier rejects with the wrong category (SIGNATURE_INVALID).

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/hybrid-mldsa-tampered
requirements.requirement: §1.3 step 5: a declared ML-DSA-65 signature that does not verify is a signature failure, although the Ed25519 signature verifies

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.1 hybrid credential whose Ed25519 signature is intact and whose ML-DSA-65 signature has been flipped by one bit after signing. The spec mandates that every declared signature verifies, so the forged post-quantum entry MUST fail verification even though the classical entry is valid. Verifier MUST REJECT with a signature-validation reason. A verifier that records ML-DSA-65 signatures as present without verifying them wrongly ACCEPTs.

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/hybrid-pq-only
requirements.requirement: §13, Cryptographic agility: a credential that declares an ML-DSA-65 signature must also carry a verifying Ed25519 signature, so an ML-DSA-65 signature alone is a signature failure

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.1 credential carrying a single ML-DSA-65 signature that verifies over JCS(TBS), and no Ed25519 signature. The spec requires a credential that declares an ML-DSA-65 entry to also carry a verifying Ed25519 entry, so a post-quantum signature alone cannot verify a credential. Verifier MUST REJECT with a signature-validation reason. A verifier that checks only that every declared signature verifies wrongly ACCEPTs.

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/no-transparency-log-index
requirements.requirement: §1.1: transparencyLogIndex is optional and outside JCS(TBS), so a v1.1 credential that omits it is accepted

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.1 credential that omits the optional transparencyLogIndex. The field is assigned by the log after signing and is outside JCS(TBS), so its absence changes no canonical bytes and no signature; this credential's JCS(TBS) is byte-identical to the v1.1 baseline's. Verifier MUST ACCEPT. A verifier that requires the field, or that reads its presence as evidence of transparency-log inclusion, wrongly REJECTs.

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/tampered-capabilities
requirements.requirement: §1.3a.4: capabilities are under the v1.1 signature, so capabilities changed after signing are a signature failure

specRefs.section: 1.3a.4 Authorization on signed fields requires v1.1
§3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.1 credential whose capabilities were escalated to include system:exec AFTER signing. Because v1.1 signs JCS(TBS), capabilities are covered by the signature; the verifier recomputes the canonical bytes, finds they no longer match, and MUST REJECT with a signature-validation reason. This is the integrity property v1.0 lacked.

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/tampered-declared-purpose
requirements.requirement: §1.5: declaredPurpose is under the v1.1 signature, so a declaredPurpose changed after signing is a signature failure

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.1 credential whose declaredPurpose.category was rewritten from financial-operations to agent-orchestration AFTER signing. Because v1.1 signs JCS(TBS) and declaredPurpose is part of it, the verifier recomputes the canonical bytes, finds they no longer match the signature, and MUST REJECT. This is the integrity property that makes a declared purpose binding and non-repudiable (§1.5).

requirements.name: atx-v1_1/untrusted-chain-authority
requirements.requirement: §1.3 step 4, key eligibility: a DID the signed issuerChain names that is not a trusted issuer contributes no eligible key, so a signature made with its key is a signature failure

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: An ATX v1.1 credential whose issuerDid is the primary authority (did:opena2a:authority:opena2a.org) and whose signed issuerChain names the primary authority and an untrusted authority (did:opena2a:authority:attacker.example). It carries one Ed25519 signature made ONLY by the untrusted authority's key over JCS(TBS), so the chain that names the signer is inside the signed bytes. The verifier trusts only the primary authority as an issuer, but the untrusted key is present in its configured public keys under a DID-URL keyId. A verifier that derives the eligible signing authorities from the credential's own issuerChain wrongly ACCEPTs: the chain names the signer's DID and the signer's key is configured. That chain is signed by the very key whose eligibility is in question, so it cannot vouch for that key. A signature verifies only against a key resolved for an authority the verifier trusts for this credential: the issuerDid, or an authority that is both named in the signed issuerChain and in the verifier's trusted issuers. A chain DID that is not a trusted issuer contributes no eligible key, so no configured key verifies the signature and the verifier MUST REJECT with a signature-validation reason.

requirements.name: atx-v1/wrong-issuer
requirements.requirement: §13, Key substitution at resolution: an issuer the verifier does not trust is rejected even when its own signature verifies

specRefs.section: §3 Hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signing, §6.1 9-factor trust scoring

requirements.description: A syntactically valid ATX signed by a real keypair, but issued under a DID that is NOT in the verifier's trusted set. The signature itself is valid; the issuer is not. Verifier MUST REJECT with an untrusted-issuer reason.
